name: Paramedic
description: Paramedics are the highest level of prehospital care — assessing and stabilising at the scene, administering drugs, managing advanced airways, reading ECGs and running a cardiac arrest before the patient reaches a hospital. ⚠ Median $60,600, reached through a certificate rather than a degree, and stacked on top of a short EMT course most people complete first. ⚠⚠ In Florida this is substantially a FIRE SERVICE credential: departments pay for it and pay extra for holding it. ⚠⚠⚠ And the accreditation rule here is the strictest on this site — the wrong programme leaves you unable to certify at all.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ Read this before you pay a programme anything. Florida requires every paramedic student to graduate from a programme accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs (CAAHEP), or one holding a Committee on Accreditation of Educational Programs for the EMS Professions (CoAEMSP) letter of review. The Department of Health states the consequence explicitly: a student entering a programme that is neither will NOT be eligible for national certification through the NREMT, NOT eligible for reciprocity in states requiring accreditation, and NOT eligible for Florida paramedic certification. ⚠⚠ That is the bluntest published statement of accreditation-outranks-credit anywhere on this site: the course can be completed, paid for and passed, and lead to nothing. ⚠ The rest of the route: Florida requires a paramedic programme of at least 700 hours of didactic and skills instruction with a skills-laboratory ratio no worse than six to one, plus a field internship aboard an advanced-life-support permitted ambulance; the cognitive examination is the NREMT; certification is issued by the Florida Department of Health Bureau of EMS under Chapter 401, Part III, not by a professional board. ⚠ Almost every programme admits certified EMTs only, so the EMT certificate comes first.
bodyHtml:
What the work actually is

O*NET, on paramedics: perform emergency cardiac care, such as cardioversion and manual defibrillation; administer drugs, orally or by injection, or perform intravenous procedures; assess nature and extent of illness or injury to establish and prioritize medical procedures; coordinate work with other emergency medical team members or police or fire department personnel; comfort and reassure patients.

⚠ The difference from an EMT is authority, not enthusiasm. The BLS puts it plainly: paramedics provide more extensive prehospital care, can administer a wider range of medications, and perform advanced airflow management and interpret electrocardiograms. An EMT stabilises and transports; a paramedic treats.

⚠⚠ You decide alone, quickly, on incomplete information, and often in someone's home at three in the morning. That is the job, and it is the part that decides whether people stay in it.

Projected need, and the wage split you need to read carefully

✅ O*NET and the BLS agree on growth. O*NET (2024–34): 101,900 paramedics employed, growth faster than average (5% to 6%), 4,900 openings a year, median $60,600 (2025). BLS (2025–35, EMTs and paramedics together): 284,100 jobs, 6% growth, +16,400.

Level2025 medianTraining
Emergency medical technician⚠ $44,470a certificate of 12 weeks to a year
Paramedic$60,600a further one to two years

⚠⚠ The step from EMT to paramedic is worth about $16,000 a year, and it is the single clearest reason to keep going rather than stopping at the short certificate.

⚠⚠⚠ Florida trains a very large number of people for this — understand where they go

Florida produced 3,661 EMS credentials in one year across 39 public institutions, the largest health training footprint in the state. Set that against 4,900 paramedic openings a year nationally and the arithmetic deserves a hard look: roughly 1,246 of Florida's credentials are at paramedic level, against a national opening count that Florida's share of population would put at perhaps 350.

⚠⚠ The resolution is that a large share of Florida paramedics are not hired as paramedics — they are hired as FIREFIGHTERS. Florida fire departments hire dual-certified Firefighter/Paramedics, and the incentives are explicit: Brevard County requires its Firefighter/EMTs to become paramedic-certified within a set period and provides the tuition; Dunedin pays a one-time $10,000 certification payment to a candidate who arrives already holding Firefighter II plus Paramedic; Palm Beach County accepts EMT or paramedic certification as an entry requirement.

⚠⚠⚠ So the honest advice is to decide early which destination you are training for, because it changes what else you need. If the answer is fire service, you also need the Florida Firefighter II certificate and the physical ability test, and the order you take them in affects your hiring and your pay. If the answer is an ambulance service or a hospital-based unit, the paramedic certificate alone is the credential — but expect competition, and expect the private ambulance sector to pay less than a municipal fire department.

⚠⚠ Take the EMT course for CREDIT if you can

Florida runs the same EMT training two ways, and the difference is invisible at enrolment:

FormCarriersWhat you get
EMS 1119 + EMS 1119L19 institutions✅ college credit that counts toward the associate degree
⚠ EMS 0110 (300 clock hours)19 institutionsa PSAV certificate carrying no college credit

⚠ Both lead to the same NREMT examination and the same state certification. Only one of them is credit you can build a degree on later, and people routinely take the clock-hour route without being told that. If there is any chance you will want the associate degree — and for promotion to supervisor or flight medic there usually is — take the credit version.

⚠ The paramedic curriculum is national; only the packaging is local

The content is set by the National EMS Education Standards, which Florida adopts by rule, so what you learn does not vary meaningfully between accredited programmes. What varies is how the modules are cut into courses, and the state numbers both schemes:

  • Three courses — EMS 2603 (modules 1–3), EMS 2604 (modules 4–5), EMS 2605 (modules 6–8), each with a laboratory.
  • Two courses — EMS 2601 (modules 1–4) and EMS 2602 (modules 5–8), or their integrated forms EMS 2601C and EMS 2602C.

⚠⚠ So a transcript comparison between two Florida paramedics can look completely different while describing identical training. The prefix carries 229 numbers across 40 institutions and the most widely shared reaches only 19 of them. Transfer on the certificate and the NREMT registration, not on course numbers — and if you must move mid-programme, expect to repeat rather than transfer, because these are lock-step cohorts built around clinical placements.

⚠ Clinical and field hours are the real schedule

Florida requires a field internship aboard an ALS-permitted ambulance, and programmes add hospital rotations on top. These are shifts, not classes — nights, weekends and whole days, at whatever service has agreed to host you, and often an hour's drive away.

⚠⚠ Expect background screening, immunisations, drug screening and current certifications to be complete before the first shift, and expect the internship to be the part that decides whether you finish: it is where most of the attrition happens, and it is very hard to combine with full-time work.

Necessary skills

  • Assessment under time pressure. Deciding what is wrong, with no chart, no laboratory and a family in the room.
  • Pharmacology you can recall cold. Doses and contraindications are not something you look up while someone is arresting.
  • ECG interpretation. The skill that most separates the paramedic from the EMT, and the one most worth over-preparing.
  • Physical durability and lifting technique. Back injuries end careers in this field more reliably than anything clinical.
  • Emotional regulation, and a plan for it. You will attend deaths, including children's. Programmes that talk about this openly are better programmes.

Advice

⚠⚠ Verify CAAHEP accreditation or a CoAEMSP letter of review in writing before you enrol. This is the one place on this site where the accreditation rule is published with its consequence attached: without it you cannot sit the NREMT and cannot be certified in Florida. Ask for it by name and check it yourself.

⚠ Start as an EMT and work a while before committing. It is a few months and it puts you on an ambulance, which is the only way to find out whether the work suits you. Many paramedic programmes want that experience anyway.

⚠ Decide about the fire service deliberately, and early. If a municipal fire department is the goal, find out now what your target departments require, in what order, and whether they will pay for the paramedic programme once you are hired — several will, and that changes the economics of the whole decision.

And ask each programme its NREMT first-attempt pass rate and its attrition rate. Accredited programmes track both and will tell you. The gap between programmes on those two numbers is much wider than the gap in what they teach.

programs.note: The programme itself — 39 Florida public institutions, the largest health training footprint in the state, stacked as a short EMT certificate and then the paramedic programme. ⚠ Read its degrees note before enrolling: the EMT course exists as both a college-credit course and a clock-hour PSAV course, and only one of them builds toward a degree.

⚠ Not a route here, but the move many paramedics eventually make — prehospital work is hard on the body and on sleep, and nursing has more settings and better pay. ⚠⚠ The paramedic certificate gives no automatic advanced standing: some Florida colleges run a paramedic-to-RN bridge and where they do not, you start from the beginning. Ask before assuming.

⚠ Not a route here. Named because it draws on the same interests — airway, ventilation, acute deterioration — from inside the hospital instead of the roadside, pays more at entry ($82,280 against $60,600), and keeps regular building hours.

courses.reason: Emergency Medical Technician — 19 institutions, the most widely carried course in the prefix and the first rung. Assessment, airway, bleeding control, spinal care, childbirth and the legal framework of prehospital care.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠⚠ Take THIS rather than EMS0110 if there is any chance you will want the associate degree. Both lead to the same NREMT examination, but EMS1119 is college credit (19 institutions) and EMS0110 is a 300-clock-hour PSAV certificate (19 institutions) carrying none. ⚠ Three colleges carry the integrated EMS1119C instead.

courses.reason: Emergency Medical Technician Laboratory — 17 institutions, the skills half: airways, immobilisation, extrication and the practical examination stations.
Emergency Medical Technician, 300 clock hours — 19 institutions, the PSAV form of the same training, and the one most technical colleges run.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Measured in CLOCK HOURS and carrying NO college credit. It reaches the same NREMT examination and the same Florida certification, so it is a legitimate fast route into the work — but it does not count toward an associate degree, and nobody tells you that at enrolment. ⚠ Two colleges carry EMS0110C.

courses.reason: EMT Hospital and Field Experience — 9 institutions. The first supervised shifts, in an emergency department and on an ambulance, and the part of the EMT certificate that is a schedule rather than a timetable.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ A clinical course: shifts on the host service's roster, including nights and weekends, often some distance away. Background screening, immunisations, TB and drug screening and current certifications must be complete BEFORE the first shift.

courses.reason: Paramedic, modules 1–3 — 7 institutions. Preparatory content, pharmacology, airway management and patient assessment at the advanced level.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Florida numbers the SAME national paramedic curriculum two ways: as three courses (EMS2603 / 2604 / 2605, each with a laboratory) or as two (EMS2601 / 2602, or the integrated EMS2601C / 2602C). ⚠ The content is set by the National EMS Education Standards and does not meaningfully differ — only the packaging does.

courses.reason: Paramedic modules 1–3 Laboratory — 7 institutions. Intravenous access, advanced airways and drug administration practised before they are done on a patient.
Paramedic, modules 4–5 — 6 institutions. Medical emergencies and trauma at the advanced level: the cardiology, respiratory and shock content the credential exists for.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ ECG interpretation usually sits here, and it is the single hardest part of the programme for most students. Prepare for it rather than meeting it.

courses.reason: Paramedic modules 4–5 Laboratory — 6 institutions, the matching skills course.
Paramedic, modules 6–8 — 6 institutions. Special populations, obstetrics and paediatrics, and EMS operations including mass-casualty and hazardous-materials response.
Paramedic I, modules 1–4 — 5 institutions. The two-course packaging of the same national curriculum, used where a college runs the programme over two terms rather than three.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also carried as the integrated EMS2601C. Indian River's 57-credit A.S. uses EMS2601C and EMS2602C at 12 credits each — identical content to the three-course scheme, cut differently.

courses.reason: Paramedic II, modules 5–8 — 5 institutions, the second half of the two-course packaging.
Paramedic Hospital and Field Clinical I — 6 institutions. Supervised advanced practice in hospital departments and on an ALS unit, alongside the didactic courses.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Clinical hours are shifts on the host service's schedule. ⚠ Florida requires the field internship to be aboard an ADVANCED LIFE SUPPORT permitted ambulance — a basic-life-support unit does not satisfy the rule, so ask what your programme has arranged.

courses.reason: Paramedic Field Internship — 11 institutions, the second most widely carried course in the prefix and the terminal requirement. The capstone internship in which you run calls as the lead clinician under a preceptor.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠⚠ This is where most attrition happens and it is very hard to combine with full-time work. It is also the record a first employer asks about — keep the run log and the preceptor evaluations.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology II — 19 institutions. Required by the associate-degree route at Indian River with a grade of C or higher, and the physiology every drug decision rests on.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Indian River's EMS A.S. names only A&P II; other programmes require A&P I (BSC2085) as well, and 7 institutions package each half as the combined BSC2085C / BSC2086C. Check your own programme's list.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology II Laboratory — 19 institutions, the corequisite half.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. In the general-education core of the associate-degree route, and the documentation you write on every call is a legal record.
College Algebra — 36 institutions. One of the mathematics options for the associate degree, and the one that travels if you later go on to a bachelor's.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Indian River accepts Mathematical Thinking, College Algebra, Elementary Statistics or Calculus I. Drug-dose calculation is taught inside the paramedic courses, not here.
